timeline.event: Trance of the Sapphire, a black-and-white film, is released (1941, FACADE Field Report; 1943, film canister; 1945, 50 year classic marquee). (It will be one of the films showing on premiere night in 1995.)
The Atlas Theater opens on Main Street, founded by Arthur McAllistor, age 18. The Kansas City Sun, April 17, 1951, says it opened "this past weekend" and calls it "a timeless gem."
Starbot, a sci-fi film, is released. (Shown on tape on the film canister in the Film Storage room; the date is the code for the Holomax puzzle.)
Audrey in Noir is released. (Dated 1-24-68 on its film canister in the Film Storage room.)

The Atlas Theater moves from Main Street, its 1951 location, to 1100 98th Street, Kansas City, KS, its current address. (Splice Bros acquired the lot next to the theater on July 9, 1970, and is still next door at the current location.)
The Splice Bros acquire the lot adjacent to the Atlas Theater; Arthur McAllistor is still the theater's owner.

The Kansas Cosmosphere presents Arthur McAllistor with a replica of the Friendship 7 capsule, honoring his devotion to the Mercury-Atlas program and his passion for space exploration. (Letter on display in the arcade, next to the capsule.)
Splice Bros opens its space beside the theater.
The theater grows to nine screens. (In 1951 it had "a select number of intimate screening rooms.")
Melissa Hartwell writes that the theater is $6,355.86 in the red this month, with bills piling up and creditors calling; her only hope is Frank's Holomax Project.
Scavengers, an animated film, is released. (It will be the big battle scene on premiere night.)
Shaboingo is released. (Dated 1995 on its film canister in the Film Storage room.)
Projectionist Frank Roberts develops the HOLOMAX, a "High-Tech Experimental 4-Dimensional Cinemorphic Projector."
Jally Corp issues an overdue billing notice to Melissa Hartwell for concession supplies.
A handwritten note calls Frank's HOLOMAX 'a big gamble' and 'reckless,' but says they have no choice — A9 is 'hanging by a thread' — and that Arthur was finally convinced to invest in it.
Arthur leaves a voicemail for Melissa: Frank is moving too fast, using hardware that didn't pass final checks.

timeline.date: Around midnight, the week before June 29, 1995
timeline.event: Dr. Jameson Kim's team at Cormack University records a highly concentrated energy spike centered on the theater for about a minute, then gone. (Reported to Frank on June 29 at 7:27 a.m.)
Arthur leaves a voicemail for Frank: the theater is on the verge of collapse, and the Holomax is their last shot.
A POST IT on the Manager’s Office wall announces ‘SHOW TESTING! 2 AM Thurs June 29, 1995’ — a show test the night before the premiere (check Frank’s notes, reread the HOLOMAX manual).
Dr. Jameson Kim of Cormack University calls Frank about the energy spike and advises caution.

Arthur leaves a voicemail for Melissa: two creditors say they're months behind on payments, his name is listed as backup signer without his agreement, and Frank hasn't been seen since late last night.

A note in the Storage Room, dated 6/30/95, says that per Melissa all crew were to stop playing Polybius — it had been giving people headaches. Blair signed it “-Blair”; someone added “(POSER!)” to the note.

The HOLOMAX premieres. Frank has disappeared, so Melissa runs it herself; she doesn't follow Frank's steps, the gauges go dead, she blacks out, and the films come alive — the HOLOMAX’s cinemorphic energy combined with the audience’s Unified Consciousness Field, and the Scavengers come out of the screen, real. The audience vanishes; Melissa goes missing, her location unknown.
Melissa Hartwell is reading her email (the ‘Welcome, Melissa Hartwell’ banner on the email client shows her logged in).
Melissa Hartwell is reading her email again.
Containment Day: F.A.C.A.D.E. seals Atlas9, airlifting a giant enclosure over the theater compound, including the nearby Splice Bros Pizza restaurant.
Melissa escapes and is questioned by a man before catching her flight; FACADE is on the hunt for the escaped characters.
FACADE recruits a new class of agents to explore the site and uncover what really happened inside.
